name: Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B
context_scaling: Native 64K (config text_config.max_position_embeddings 65536; card states input up to 64K, output up to 64K). Sliding window 512 tokens on 35 of 42 layers.
attention_variant: Gemma-4 hybrid stack: 35 sliding_attention layers (window 512, head_dim 256, 2 KV heads) + 7 full_attention layers using the separate global geometry (global_head_dim 512). config also sets num_kv_shared_layers 18; enable_moe_block false, num_experts null - dense, not MoE.
notes: KV BASIS (derived): 7 full-attention layers x 2 (K and V) x 1 global KV head (num_global_key_value_heads is null in config, taken as 1 to match the gemma-4-12b record) x global_head_dim 512 x 2 bytes = 14336 bytes/token; the 35 sliding layers are bounded by the 512-token window and do not grow with context, so they are excluded. config's num_kv_shared_layers 18 may cut this further if a full-attention layer shares its cache; not verified against a live cache measurement. FLOPS BASIS (derived): 2 x active_params_b for a dense forward pass, using the card's 4B effective count that already excludes the per-layer embedding tables. ADDED 2026-11-04 from the trending sweep (trendingScore 114, text-generation). PARAMS: safetensors.total 7996156490 = 7.996B. The card's spec table states '8B (4B effective)', so active_params_b 4.0 is the vendor's effective count, not a derivation - Gemma-4's per-layer embedding tables (hidden_size_per_layer_input 256, vocab 262144, 128 embedding layers) carry the other ~4B and are not touched per token. IT IS A FINETUNE of google/gemma-4-E4B-it (OpenMDW-1.1, post-trained on Gemma 4), not a new base architecture: same Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration config, plus a ~150M vision and ~300M audio encoder inherited from the base. The base is NOT a catalog record, so this is ingested as its own model record rather than via mk_finetune_record.py. WHY IT EARNS A RECORD: in its own 4B-class table it beats Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma4-E4B-it on 14 of 20 rows, several by 20+ points (IHEval 84.79 vs 60.57, GaRAGe 42.61 vs 24.66, RelyToolBench 63.16 vs 43.35, When2Call 63.36 vs 37.85, RoleBench 67.05 vs 53.66). It LOSES Tau2-Bench badly (55.10 vs Qwen's 75.06), RULER 64K (86.99 vs 95.15) and LongBench v2 (50.50 vs 59.93) - the instruction-following/grounding wins do not carry over to tool-use state tracking or long-context retrieval. All rows are NVIDIA's own runs on their NeMo Gym harness, so they are vendor_claim and not comparable to third-party harness numbers for the same benchmark names elsewhere in the catalog. SIZING for a low-VRAM box: 8.0B parameters x 0.5 GiB/B = 4.0 GiB at bf16, ~2.2 GiB at Q4_K_M. NVIDIA ships a pre-built Q4_K_M ('-4GB' repo) and the card prints the quantised column too (RoleBench 71.21 at Q4 vs 67.05 bf16; Tau2 52.32 vs 55.10).
